evidence_quotes.quote: framework for redesigning informal settlements based on Low-impact Design and Development methodology
It involves the management of rainwater through the implementation of urban infrastructure on local scale in a decentralized and collaborative manner.
The stages envisaged in the framework are: (i) initial, which involves approaching the community, establishing bonds and setting up a management group, (ii) diagnosis, and (iii) project.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the literal/plain Criterion 2 reading result in exclusion. Even if setting up a community management group in an action-research project were viewed generously under broad governance wording, the paper focuses on Low-Impact Design rainwater/stormwater urban redesign for hydrological stress resilience in marshlands rather than household or community drinking water or sanitation service access (C1 and C4 fail), and does not examine legal, administrative, regulatory, or institutional access mechanisms.
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E07 wrong service). The paper presents an Action-Research methodological framework for urban redesign of marshland informal settlements using Low-Impact Design and Development (LID) for local rainwater/stormwater management and resilience to hydrological stress, rather than household or community drinking water or sanitation service access. Moreover, it proposes a participatory urban design workflow (community engagement, diagnosis, project design) rather than empirically evaluating legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanisms governing water or sanitation access outcomes.
